units.notes: The 2024 Resource Evaluation Study supports the capacity and the 2031 start year already in GEM, but names no site, turbine maker, or city. I found nothing newer that names this unit.

qa.recommendation: The study rounds each turbine to 233 MW. GEM shows 232.5 MW, which may come from a different filing. Keep 232.5 MW unless the reviewer prefers the study's figure.
qa.note: The preferred portfolio table in the 2024 study says 233 MW for the 2031 turbine. I did not find a source that says 232.5 MW.

qa.recommendation: The two turbines the study dates to 2028 and 2029 appear to be the Orient Energy Center in Adair County, which GEM should hold as its own plant. This placeholder is the 2031 turbine and is a different unit.
qa.note: A 2025 news report and MidAmerican's fact sheet describe Orient as about 465 MW in two turbines for 2028. I did not find a named site for the 2031 turbine.

monitor.monitor_reason: The turbine is an unsited planning placeholder with no filing yet.
monitor.note: Watch Iowa Utilities Commission generating certificate filings for a named project of this size.

source_log.note: MidAmerican's 2024 Resource Evaluation Study, filed November 2024, lists a 233 MW simple-cycle combustion turbine in 2031 in its preferred portfolio table. That matches GEM's start year of 2031. The study does not name a site, so this is an unsited placeholder. The plan is already cited for this unit, so there is nothing new to add.
